content:
Aiyana Brooks-Tan
Junior Frontend Developer | React • TypeScript • Node.js
Dublin, Ireland | aiyana.brookstan@example.com | +353 55 555 0404
github.com/aiyana-bt-example | aiyana-bt.example.com

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Junior developer with hands-on experience building accessible web applications using React and TypeScript, including a software development internship and freelance work. Developed a full-stack final-year project using Node.js, Express and PostgreSQL, and has experience writing unit tests with Jest and React Testing Library. First Class Honours graduate in Computing – Software Development, with a strong focus on accessible, user-centred interfaces.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Frontend: React, TypeScript, JavaScript, Next.js, HTML5, CSS3, Tailwind CSS
Backend and data: Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL
Testing and tools: Jest, React Testing Library, Storybook, Git/GitHub, Figma
Other: Web accessibility (WCAG 2.1)

EXPERIENCE
Frontend Developer (Part-time, Freelance) | Self-employed | Oct 2025–Present
- Built a booking website for a local yoga studio using Next.js and Tailwind CSS, with class timetable and booking requests sent by email.
- Deployed the website on Vercel and set up content editing through Markdown files.
- Completed small updates for two WordPress sites.

Teaching Assistant, First-Year Web Development Lab | Liffey Institute of Technology | Spring 2025
- Supported approximately 30 students during one semester of first-year web development labs.

Software Development Intern | Harbourline Media, Dublin | May 2024–Aug 2024
- Worked with the web team on the company’s React news site.
- Fixed accessibility audit issues involving keyboard navigation, colour contrast and ARIA labels across 20+ components.
- Built a reusable, keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery and documented it with Storybook stories.
- Wrote unit tests using Jest and React Testing Library.

Barista (Part-time during studies) | Corner Bean Cafe, Dublin | 2021–2025

PROJECTS
Tidewatch — Final-Year Project | 2024–2025
- Built an accessible web app for sea swimmers displaying tides, water temperature and weather around the Irish coast.
- Developed the frontend with React and TypeScript, and a Node.js/Express API that caches data from public weather and tide APIs; used PostgreSQL for user favourites.
- Tested the app with NVDA and VoiceOver; achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100.
- Received 82% (First Class) and demonstrated the project at the college showcase.
- Technologies: React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Chart.js, Jest.

Yoga Studio Booking Site | Freelance | 2025
- Created marketing pages and a class timetable, with booking requests sent by email.
- Technologies: Next.js, React, Tailwind CSS, Vercel.

Study Buddy — Group Project | 2023
- Built the React frontend and login screens for a four-person team project: a web app matching classmates for study sessions.
- Technologies: React, JavaScript, Firebase Authentication.

OTHER ACHIEVEMENTS AND VOLUNTEERING
- Second place, student hackathon (2024): developed the frontend for a transit delay notifier in a three-person team over 24 hours.
- Run social media for a sea swimming club.

EDUCATION
BSc (Hons) Computing – Software Development | Liffey Institute of Technology | 2021–2025
First Class Honours
Relevant modules: Web Development, Databases, Human-Computer Interaction, Software Testing, Data Structures & Algorithms

LANGUAGES
English (native) | Mandarin (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a clear, well-structured, professional CV with strong evidence for a junior frontend or junior full-stack profile. The Professional Summary is targeted, the skills are grouped logically, and the experience and project bullets contain credible technical detail and measurable outcomes, including 20+ components, approximately 30 students, a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100, and an 82% final-year grade. The CV demonstrates a coherent progression from academic projects to internship and freelance work. Its main content limitation is not poor writing but the distinction between the candidate's current junior-level experience and the job's more senior 2+ years requirement.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly overall: it uses conventional section headings, readable chronological entries, standard text-based formatting, and relevant keywords including React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Jest, React Testing Library, Git/GitHub, Next.js, Storybook, accessibility, and WCAG 2.1. It should have a moderate-to-high AI/ATS screening probability for junior frontend searches, but a lower probability for this specific role because the ad's strongest filters are 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience, end-to-end testing, and security fundamentals. The document mentions unit testing clearly but does not distinguish that the candidate lacks end-to-end testing experience. It also does not expose Firebase Authentication, which is useful evidence for the authentication aspect of the role. Avoid adding unsupported keywords such as Playwright, NestJS, Docker, AWS, OWASP, or healthcare privacy.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with the role's React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, accessibility, Next.js, Storybook, Git, and wellness-related requirements. Tidewatch is particularly relevant because it combines an accessible patient-adjacent user experience, a Node.js API, PostgreSQL, API integration, screen-reader testing, and a strong accessibility result. The yoga studio project supports the ad's wellness experience preference, and the Teaching Assistant experience supports the mentoring expectation. The principal fit gaps are that the candidate's material does not demonstrate 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience, automated end-to-end testing, OWASP/security fundamentals, Docker or AWS, analytics/A/B testing, or German/Croatian. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than defects that can be solved through wording. The CV should nevertheless make the candidate's relevant authentication, accessibility, backend, testing, and mentoring evidence as visible as possible.
critique.improvement_instructions:
Priority improvements:
1. In the PROJECTS section under “Study Buddy — Group Project,” add the supported detail: “Built the React frontend and login screens using Firebase Authentication for a four-person team project.” This makes the candidate’s authentication exposure visible without claiming broader security or OWASP expertise.
2. In the TECHNICAL SKILLS section, add “Firebase Authentication” under “Backend and data” or create a separate “Authentication” entry. This is supported by the candidate’s Study Buddy project and improves keyword coverage for the job’s authentication requirement.
3. In the PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY, change “has experience writing unit tests with Jest and React Testing Library” to “has experience writing automated unit tests with Jest and React Testing Library.” This uses the job’s terminology accurately while avoiding any implication that the candidate has end-to-end testing experience.
4. In the PROJECTS section under “Tidewatch — Final-Year Project,” retain the existing API and PostgreSQL details but make the third-party integration more explicit by changing “a Node.js/Express API that caches data from public weather and tide APIs” to “a Node.js/Express API that integrates with and caches data from public weather and tide APIs.”
5. In the EXPERIENCE section under “Teaching Assistant, First-Year Web Development Lab,” change the bullet to “Supported approximately 30 students during one semester of first-year web development labs, answering questions and helping them progress through web development exercises.” The added wording is supported by the teaching-assistant role and better surfaces evidence relevant to mentoring junior colleagues.
6. In the PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY, keep the junior positioning but make the role match more precise by changing “Junior developer” to “Junior frontend/full-stack developer.” This accurately reflects the React frontend work and Node.js/PostgreSQL project experience without overstating professional backend experience.
7. Do not add Playwright, end-to-end testing, NestJS, AWS, Docker, OWASP Top 10, healthcare privacy, German, Croatian, analytics, or A/B testing to the CV. The supplied candidate information does not support those claims.
